obernants.approximation_semantics: Conditional source relation; exact finite algebra where declared, otherwise candidate inner complement or ambiguous converse
obernants.assumptions: Fixed corpus, indexes, order state and successful I/O; acyclic ancestry; unforgeable stamp is not assumed
obernants.domain: Finite valid stores and ID vectors; precise specialization in operator
obernants.observation_scope: One ordered selection or saved-set load transition
obernants.operator: Universe: ordered duplicate-free candidate vectors, valid k and seed, and output vectors. Candidate inner complement includes sampled outputs longer than min(k,n), unsorted outputs, duplicate outputs, and IDs absent from candidates. This is a conditional source model of the sample stage, not the complement of the full query.

obernants.operator: Fix k and seed. A sampled observation Y has every ordered candidate vector C whose first min(k,|C|) pairs in sorted(key(C position,seed) xor id salt,id) have numerically sorted selected IDs equal to Y as compatible antecedents. Different candidate orders and losing candidates remain possible. No unique inverse; k=0 maps every candidate vector to empty.

obernants.operator: The xorshift stream advances per candidate position. Removing one eligible ID changes ranks of later unchanged IDs as well as competition for k slots. Changed-ID dictionaries therefore do not bound output membership changes. Historical witness eligible [0,1,2] to [0,2], C={1}, pred>=1 sample=1/2 gives old [1], fresh [2], legacy merge []; repaired load must return [2].

obernants.operator: Hold query order and seed fixed, replace legacy delta-merge by complete target selection for stale sampled queries. Output equals F even if O\C differs from F\C. This intervention fixes candidate coupling but does not validate feature extraction, mutable same-hash indexes or forged stable stamps. Oracle compares repaired witness and rejects historical empty result.
